optimizedContext.value:
# Specs Deps CLI

## Rules

- Command group `specd specs deps`; every subcommand accepts `--format text|json|toon` (default text).
- Signatures: `list <spec-id>`, `add <spec-id> --dep <dependency-id>...`, `remove <spec-id> --dep <dependency-id>...`, `set <spec-id> --dep <dependency-id>...`, `clear <spec-id>`.
- `list` → `Kernel.specs.getPersistedDeps`, print `dependsOn`. Uninitialized spec: MUST report not-initialized rather than indistinguishable empty list; text distinguishes cases, JSON/TOON include `initialized` field.
- `add` → `Kernel.specs.updatePersistedDeps` with `add` = supplied IDs; print resulting persisted list.
- `remove` → `remove` = supplied IDs; print result. Uninitialized state: report no-op outcome, not error.
- `set` → `set` = supplied IDs (may be empty to clear via set); print result.
- `clear` → `clear: true`; print resulting empty list.
- Handlers MUST NOT implement add/remove/set merge semantics, initial-state derivation, or persisted-state writes. Every mutation = one `updatePersistedDeps` call, flags mapped directly onto `UpdatePersistedSpecDepsInput`.
- Error mapping, exit code 1 with `error:` message: `SpecNotFoundError` names unresolved spec; `ArtifactConflictError` reports concurrent modification, instruct retry; `ReadOnlyWorkspaceError` gives no configuration workaround (per core:workspace readOnly error-message conventions).

## Constraints

- Never read/write spec-lock.json directly; every operation flows through Kernel.specs.getPersistedDeps / Kernel.specs.updatePersistedDeps.
- Distinct from change scope editing (`change edit --add-spec`): operates on canonical persisted state, not draft specDependsOn.
- Every leaf subcommand calls `.allowExcessArguments(false)`
